text:
elaine: Heads-up: customer on CF Workers hit a hard build error when importing the SDK. esbuild via wrangler fails with "could not resolve 'fs'" and TS points at Node types. We need a crisp guidance and a low-friction distro for edge runtimes. Any suggestions?

omar: This is a common pattern. The shortest path: publish a dedicated edge subpath (eg `redwood-inference/edge`) that is ESM-only and has zero Node built-ins. Then update docs so Workers users import that.

ben: Agree. Practically that means we must produce dist/edge.mjs + dist/edge.d.ts that only reference DOM types (ReadableStream, AbortSignal) and a fetch-based transport. No node timers, no fs/net imports.

elaine: Can we do this with package.json exports so bundles auto-resolve it? People hate adding flags to wrangler.

omar: Yes. Add an exports mapping for the subpath. Example I like:
```
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" },
  "./edge": { "import": "./dist/edge.mjs", "types": "./dist/edge.d.ts" }
},
"browser": { "debug": false }
```
That way `import { createEdgeClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge'` pulls only the edge code.

ben: Types nuance: TS sometimes picks up the root d.ts even when you import a subpath. To be extra safe add `types` top-level that points to an index that re-exports edge types OR use `typesVersions` to map older TS consumers. But primarily docs should encourage the subpath import.

elaine: What about retry loops and timers? Some code calls `setImmediate` or `process.nextTick` in our backoff util which blows up in Workers.

omar: Replace those with a tiny runtime wrapper:
```
const defer = (fn) => (globalThis.setImmediate ? globalThis.setImmediate(fn) : globalThis.setTimeout(fn, 0));
```
And avoid any direct `process.*` references. Use environment-injected config rather than reading `process.env` at runtime.

ben: Crypto: Workers have `crypto.getRandomValues`. Some customers try to call `crypto.randomBytes`. Offer an exported helper in the edge build:
```
export function randomBytes(n){ const arr = new Uint8Array(n); crypto.getRandomValues(arr); return arr; }
```
Document that it returns Uint8Array on edge, not Node Buffer.

elaine: Wranger-specific workaround I used yesterday for a one-off customer:
```
# wrangler.toml build.command
esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --outfile=dist/worker.js --platform=browser --format=esm --define:process.env.NODE_ENV='"production"' --external:fs --external:net
```
But that's terrible DX. We should avoid making users do that.

omar: Totally. Exports + edge bundle eliminates need for externals. Also consider adding `sideEffects:false` and a small rollup/esbuild plugin in our build to ensure node-only modules are not pulled into the edge entry.

ben: Header size gotcha: Cloudflare strictly limits header size. During dev we attach verbose debug metadata headers. Ensure edge client avoids sending large JSON in headers by default and gate debug headers on an opt-in flag.

edge-bot: note: internal branch `edge-entrypoint-proto` exists with dist/edge.mjs and simplified transport. CI: esbuild edge bundle OK.

elaine: Good. Docs: please add a Workers Quickstart + snippet like:
```
import { createEdgeClient } from 'redwood-inference/edge';
const client = createEdgeClient({ url: REDWOOD_URL, apiKey: SECRET });
addEventListener('fetch', e => e.respondWith(handle(e.request)));
async function handle(req){ const res = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' }); return new Response(res.text); }
```
And troubleshooting checklist: tsconfig lib: ["dom"], use subpath import, if bundling errors check exports/browser fields.

omar: Also add a short migration note for library maintainers: how to move transitive debug/logger code behind dynamic import or optional dependency so it doesn't pollute the edge bundle. Dynamic import + top-level await (for ESM) works well for lazy dev-only features.

ben: One more: telemetry. Add an opt-in telemetry ping when `createEdgeClient` is instantiated so we can measure adoption before removing heavy deps from the main entry. Make it opt-in and privacy-friendly.

elaine: I'll draft the README and a tiny `workers-starter` repo with wrangler config and link the PR to `edge-entrypoint-proto`. Thanks y'all.

omar: I'll open the PR to add the `exports` mapping + edge typings and scrub node timers.

ben: I'll add the docs snippet and a short note on guarding debug headers. Good progress. :thumbsup:
